pages.text: Energy Cells act as the grid's buffer, separating generation from consumption so that an intermittent generator does not starve the machines.$(br2)$(bold)Basic Cell:$(reset)$(li)Capacity: $(bold)500 million$(reset) AE$(li)Transfer: up to 1 million AE/tick in or out (shared charge/discharge limit)$(br2)Tier comparison follows on the next page. A Portable Cell placed in the charge slot is recharged by the cell.

$(bold)Three storage tiers$(reset) (capacity / per-tick transfer):$(li)Basic: 500 million / 1 million$(li)Advanced: 2 billion / 5 million$(li)Super: 20 billion / 50 million$(br2)Advanced and Super are crafted by upgrading the tier below, and tiers can be mixed in one grid.$(br2)The transfer limit determines burst throughput; if generators and pipes are faster, the cell becomes the bottleneck.$(br2)For capacity beyond a single cell, see the $(l:akaishi:cell_serializer)Cell Serializer$(/l).

Storing is one part of the grid. Start with $(l:akaishi:energy_basics)Akaishi Energy Basics$(/l), then connect the $(l:akaishi:generator)Energy Generator$(/l) or $(l:akaishi:gen_matrix)Generator Matrix$(/l) to $(l:akaishi:energy_pipe)Energy Pipes$(/l) to complete the loop. Scale up with the $(l:akaishi:cell_serializer)Cell Serializer$(/l) and carry $(l:akaishi:portable_cell)Portable Cells$(/l) when away from the base.
